caption.text:
Brumbies are being shot from the air. Listen to a live interview here in Australia with @ashleyavis.

We are on the ground in Sydney to document the aerial cull of thousands of iconic brumbies.

These wild horses, which live in and around Kosciuszko National Park, are being shot from helicopters in an operation ordered by the New South Wales government.

The cull has ignited intense debate across Australia and around the world, with many questioning the population estimates being used to justify the killing of one of Australia’s most iconic animals.

“This isn’t humane management,” says Avis. “If we want to talk about humane management, let’s sit down at the table to do that. But this issue, what’s happening with the culling - which is a very convenient and gentle word for killing - this is wrong, this is black and white, let’s come together to stop this.”

For detailed updates on this issue, follow @brumby_strong, and reach out to those in power by calling and tagging:

Penny Sharpe @pennysharpemlc
Chris Minns @chrisminnsmp
National Parks NSW @nswnationalparks
Anthony Albanese @albomp

As Avis concludes, “Penny Sharpe is the New South Wales Minister for Environment and Heritage… how an individual with such a title could order the violent massacre of brumbies who are part of Australia’s heritage is, in a word, shocking.”
